title: Rosie McHargue and players with no school of their own
summary: Neither man has information on Rosie's influence; both see him as competent without a distinct individuality.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Who was the clarinetist with Ted Weems for a while, who got into Dixie working? Rosie McCard.

Yeah. Rosie, I'm sure, did a lot of record listening. His arrangements, for example, are rearrangements of Memphis Five, an original Dixieland jazz band and so forth. And have you any information about Rosie, where his influence or enthusiasm might have went?
Not at all. I'm sorry, John. I don't seem to be providing much help. Well, would you say that?

No, that's fine. Because in my own mind, Rosie turned out to be a competent musician without individuality or without copying one person so that he can be classified in a school, or without developing an individuality which makes him the founder of a school.
My feeling is along the same lines, yes.
